reapack.name: REAPER MCP
reapack.desc: REAPER MCP — Model Context Protocol interface (immersive/spatial audio)

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
The true-peak interpolator is now our own design, and the estimator says all four of its bounds as numbers.
WHAT CHANGES.
The true-peak estimator replaces the ITU-R BS.1770-4 Annex 2 table (12 taps at 4x oversampling -- the Recommendation's minimum) with a 24-tap, 8x polyphase interpolator designed for this product. Measured the same way on the same EBU programme material, every window read in the context of its file against an exact reference: the worst under-read falls from 0.52 dB to 0.14 dB (SQAM 27, castanets) and the worst over-read from 0.22 dB to 0.10 dB (SQAM 64); the standard's own fs/4 test tones read 0.13 dB low, inside Tech 3341's window. `truePeakDb` MOVES on real material -- that is the point of the change.
Every disclosed bound followed the table, because each is computed from it at first call rather than written down: `truePeakGridBoundDb` 0.169 dB (was 0.688), `truePeakFilterGainBoundDb` +0.086 dB (was +0.222), `truePeakEdgeGuardSamples` 12 (was 6; it is taps/2).
TWO NEW FIELDS complete the disclosure in numbers, on every payload that carries the others: `truePeakFilterLossBoundDb` (0.088 dB) -- how far the interpolation filter itself can read a sine low within its passband, beyond what the grid misses; and `truePeakSineLowBoundDb` (0.127 dB, reached at a quarter of the sample rate) -- the estimator's actual worst under-read of a steady sine with the grid, the filter's loss and its phase error all in, tighter than the sum of the two. The passband edge ships as a constant (0.45 of the sample rate) beside the table.
THE BOUNDS ARE FOR A SINE, and the description says so: for a sine inside the passband the interior reading is never lower than the truth minus `truePeakSineLowBoundDb` and never higher than the truth plus `truePeakFilterGainBoundDb`.
COST. The meter now runs one interpolation pass for both true-peak numbers where it ran two. Measured on a machine a load witness certified quiet for the whole run, the new meter call takes 3.49x the previous one -- about 0.4 s per minute of audio at 48 kHz, one channel, where the previous meter spent 0.11 s.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
The true-peak reading now tells you how much it cannot see -- on BOTH sides.
Version 1.19.0 disclosed how far the estimator's evaluation grid can read a sine BELOW the truth, and said in words that the interpolation filter's own error was not covered. That error has now been measured, against an exact reference, on the EBU's published programme material, with every window read in the context of its file rather than cut out of it: the estimator can also read ABOVE the truth, by up to 0.22 dB on Euroradio material.
WHAT CHANGES.
Every payload that already reported `truePeakGridBoundDb` now reports `truePeakFilterGainBoundDb` beside it: the most a reading can sit above the truth for a sine, computed from the filter's own coefficients at first call rather than written down as a number, so it cannot drift away from the code that produces it. For the Recommendation's table it is 0.222 dB, reached near a quarter of the sample rate.
THE BOUND SHIPS WITH ITS SCOPE. It is an OVER-read bound for the INTERIOR reading (`truePeakDbInterior`): at a raw window edge `truePeakDb` can exceed it by the edge ring that `truePeakEdgeDominated` already flags. It does not bound the filter's LOSS on the low side, and it is derived for a sine -- a broadband transient can exceed it slightly.
THE DESCRIPTION NOW STATES THE MEASURED WORST CASES WITH THEIR PROVENANCE, replacing the single figure 1.19.0 carried ("about 0.13 dB low", measured on a synthesised signal against a reference later shown not to have converged): the standard's own true-peak test signals read up to 0.30 dB low (EBU Tech 3341 case 17, inside the standard's tolerance); programme material reads up to 0.52 dB LOW (SQAM 27, castanets) and up to 0.22 dB HIGH (Euroradio 05), all against an exact reference on the EBU's published files. A professional can bracket a reading from both sides and judge whether the tolerance meets their standard, or reach for a more accurate tool.
`truePeakDb` itself is unchanged: the header was compiled before and after and read IDENTICAL over the same 12 fixtures as 1.19.0.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
The true-peak reading now tells you how much it cannot see.
A true peak is the highest point a sound reaches BETWEEN your samples, and it is found by reconstructing the waveform and inspecting it on a grid of points. Inseglet's estimator inspects every quarter of a sample -- the minimum ITU-R BS.1770-4 allows -- so the nearest point it looks at can sit an eighth of a sample away from a real inter-sample maximum, and the number it reports falls BELOW the truth by an amount that grows with frequency. It errs in the unsafe direction: it reports headroom that is not there.
WHAT CHANGES.
Every payload that already reported `truePeakEdgeGuardSamples` now reports two more fields beside it. `truePeakOversampling` is the grid factor in use. `truePeakGridBoundDb` is how far a full-band sine peak can fall below the truth FROM THE GRID ALONE. The bound is computed from the factor rather than written down as a number, so it cannot drift away from the code that produces it.
THE BOUND SHIPS WITH ITS SCOPE, because a bound whose scope is not stated is a claim rather than a measurement. It covers the evaluation grid ONLY. It EXCLUDES the interpolation filter's own magnitude error, so the total shortfall on real material can exceed it, and it is derived for a sine.
`truePeakDb` itself is unchanged. The header was compiled before and after the change and read IDENTICAL over 12 fixtures, all five EBU Tech 3341 true-peak signals included.
AND THE METER IS NOW MEASURED AGAINST ALL NINE OF THOSE SIGNALS RATHER THAN FIVE. Cases 20 to 23, read from the EBU's own published Loudness test set rather than synthesised in-process, read -0.130183, -0.078912, -0.204110 and -0.078911 dBTP against an expected 0.0 -- every one inside the +0.2/-0.4 dB window Tech 3341 sets.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
Every true-peak reading now says whether it came from the edge of the window you asked for, and the meter reports the window it actually rendered.
A true peak is measured by reconstructing what sits BETWEEN your samples. At the two ends of any window that reconstruction has nothing to reach into, so the filter rings against the silence outside -- and the number you get can sit up to about 0.9 dB above what the material contains, purely because of where you put the window. Version 1.17.0 disclosed that in `analysis.meter`.
WHAT CHANGES.
Every tool that reports a true peak now discloses it. `analysis.read_samples`, `analysis.accessor_meter`, `analysis.stem_loudness`, `analysis.dialog_loudness`, `analysis.downmix_check`, `analysis.object_loudness` and `analysis.binaural_check` each report `truePeakDbInterior` -- the same maximum with both window edges excluded -- and `truePeakEdgeDominated`, true when the peak came ONLY from an edge, beside the `truePeakDb` they already reported. `truePeakDb` itself is unchanged: measured on two builds over the same calls, it moved by 0.000000 dB on every one. On a steady tone read through the accessor path, the reported true peak moves 0.70 dB across 24 one-sample window offsets while the interior figure moves 0.05.
`analysis.meter` now reports the window it actually rendered. REAPER quantises render bounds, so a window asked for in samples may not be the window measured. The new `window` block reports what was requested beside what was rendered, the difference in samples, and a `snapped` flag, and warns when they differ. No grid size is asserted: ask for a few more samples and watch `renderedFrames` move.
The server now says which build is answering. `initialize`'s `serverInfo.build.uuid` is the identity of the code actually running, not of the file on disk, so replacing the plug-in without restarting REAPER is now visible instead of silent. The discovery file carries it too.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
The true-peak meter now uses the interpolation filter ITU-R BS.1770-4 publishes, and keeps the sample peak as a floor.
`analysis.meter`'s per-channel `truePeakDb` -- and the mid/side and downmix reports that share it -- oversample 4x, as BS.1770-4 Annex 2 describes. Until now the interpolator was a short Hann-windowed sinc. It reads inside the +0.2/-0.4 dB tolerance EBU Tech 3341 sets on every one of its true-peak test signals, so nothing you measured was out of tolerance -- but it droops in the top octave, and on dense, bright material it recovered less of the inter-sample peak than the Recommendation's own filter does: about 0.15 dB less at 44.1 kHz on a nine-partial test chord, and always low.
WHAT CHANGES. The interpolator is now the 48-tap, 4-phase filter tabulated in BS.1770-4 Annex 2, coefficient for coefficient, so the reading agrees with meters built on that table. The input sample itself is kept as a floor, because the table alone can read a sample-aligned peak up to 0.2 dB below the sample, and a true peak below the sample peak is not a reading anyone should act on.
What you will notice: on bright, dense masters `truePeakDb` reads a little higher than before -- a few hundredths to about 0.15 dB -- and it is the more accurate figure. On a steady tone the reading can move either way by up to about 0.3 dB depending on the frequency and on where the peak falls between samples: up near 0.4x the sample rate, where the old filter was weakest, and down around a sixth of the sample rate, where the Recommendation's filter has its own small dip. Both are inside the published tolerance. The deliverable gate (`analysis.check_deliverable`) is unchanged -- it has always used REAPER's own true-peak engine.
The unit tests now include Tech 3341's five true-peak signals at the published tolerance, so the meter's conformance is tested on every build rather than assumed.
No tools were added or removed.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
The meter was measuring at your sound card's rate, not your project's -- and the ADM export was shipping files labelled with it.
REAPER's render engine follows the audio device. Unless you have asked REAPER to request a specific rate, the device runs at whatever rate it likes, and every render follows it -- including the temporary renders this extension uses to measure loudness and to author deliverables. If your project says 48 kHz and your interface is running at 44.1, the numbers you were reading, and the files you were writing, were 44.1.
Nothing was lying. `analysis.meter` reported its figures honestly, `spatial.export_adm` wrote the rate it actually rendered at into both the WAV header and the ADM metadata, and the project setting reported the project setting. There was simply nothing anywhere that compared the two numbers.
WHAT CHANGES. The analysis and deliverable renders are now REQUESTED at the project's sample rate instead of following the engine. On a correctly configured machine nothing changes at all. On a machine where the device is running at another rate:
* `analysis.meter` now measures what your project actually is. True peak is the figure that moves -- it is oversampled from the rendered samples, so the rate it was rendered at matters. * `spatial.export_adm` with `profile: "dolby-atmos"` stops refusing a project that is already at 48 kHz. It used to refuse with "set the project sample rate to 48000", which was no help if you had already done exactly that. * `spatial.export_adm` on its default settings stops silently writing a master at the wrong rate. It now warns when the rendered rate is not the project's, and every rate refusal in the extension names the real cause -- including your audio device's rate when it can read it.
`analysis.meter` and `analysis.revive_and_meter` also report `rate.requested` (what the render was asked for) and `rate.device` (your audio interface's own rate, when REAPER's device is open), so you can see where a disagreement comes from rather than guessing.
IF YOU WANT THE OLD BEHAVIOUR, ASK FOR IT BY NAME. Both tools take `renderRate`: `"project"` is the new default, `"follow"` is the previous behaviour, and a number forces a specific rate. Nothing is taken away.
ONE THING THIS DOES NOT FIX. Forcing the render rate means REAPER resamples. That is the right trade for a measurement that has to describe your deliverable, but it is a resample, and the extension says so in a warning rather than leaving you to work it out.
No tools were added or removed.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
A meter that can only read a dead source now has a sibling that may revive it.
`analysis.meter` refuses to report a silence its two read paths disagree about: when the audio accessor returns an empty window while the source is online, it reports the disagreement instead of a level, and tells you to run REAPER's own "rebuild peaks" action. That refusal is correct and it is unchanged in this release, byte for byte.
What it could not do is act. `analysis.revive_and_meter` is a SEPARATE tool that may: it revives the dead read path and reads again, then reports the meter it got.
WHY A SEPARATE TOOL AND NOT A FLAG. MCP tool annotations are static per tool. A `revive: true` parameter would make `analysis.meter` a tool whose `readOnly: true` annotation is a lie on exactly the calls that matter -- and a client that refuses mutating tools by annotation alone would be given no way to tell. So `analysis.meter` keeps `readOnly: true` AND keeps its refusal, and the permission to mutate lives in a tool your client can decline without reading a single argument.
It reuses `analysis.meter`'s handler by registry lookup and re-implements nothing, so the two tools cannot drift apart in what they measure.
It does not pretend to restore. `revive.restored` reports `false` with a reason: source revalidation is not a snapshotted project field, so the tool declines to claim a repair it cannot observe.
Surface 191 tools / 4 resources / 5 prompts -- the first tool added since 1.12.0.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
Fourteen more tools say what they adjusted, and one had nothing to say.
1.13.3 gave `track.set_channels` a `clamped` flag and a `warnings` line. Fourteen more mutating tools carry it now, declared in each tool's output schema and listed as required.
NINE INPUT CLAMPERS -- transport.set_playrate, track.set_rec_mon, track.set_rec_mode, track.set_folder, item.set_position, item.set_length, item.set_fade_in, item.set_fade_out, take.set_pan -- name what was ASKED and what was USED. The comparison is against the caller's own value, never an intermediate, so a value adjusted twice reports the distance it travelled.
FIVE PER-NOTE PINS -- midi.apply_groove, humanize, nudge, quantize, stretch -- report a COUNT. They do not adjust an input: the argument is honoured exactly and some notes still cannot land where it implies, so they pin to the item start. "Requested X, used Y" would be false for these.
Nothing about any adjustment itself changed. This release changes what callers are TOLD, not what REAPER is given. `required` grows on fourteen tools, which is why this is a minor bump.
spatial.set_source_position was examined and deliberately left alone: it was listed among the silent adjusters and is not one -- the construct behind that listing is an FX-index lookup fallback. The declared bounds are still not enforced; a tool tells you it clamped your value, it does not refuse it.
Surface 190 tools / 4 resources / 5 prompts -- UNMOVED. ctest 29 -> 30, one added.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
A mutating tool now reports the input it silently adjusted.
`track.set_channels` clamps a request below 2 up to 2, clamps above 64 down to 64, and rounds an odd count upward -- and it returned `{"ok": true, "channels": N}` with nothing naming any of it, so a caller that trusted `ok` could not see that it had not been given what it asked for. It now returns `clamped` and a `warnings` line naming what was asked and what was set, both declared in its output schema. Nothing about the adjustment itself changed.
The reporting shape is the one this binary already shipped elsewhere: `warnings` as the `spatial.*` tools use it, `clamped` as the accessor tools declare it. Fifteen other mutating tools still adjust their inputs silently and are unchanged here.
Surface 190 tools / 4 resources / 5 prompts -- UNMOVED. ctest 28 -> 29, one added.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
Documentation release: the standards basis now says WHICH loudness engine implements which revision of ITU-R BS.1770, and two public claims that were false are corrected. No functional change.
`docs/CONVENTIONS.md` said "Standards basis throughout: ... ITU-R BS.1770-5". TWO loudness paths ship and they cite different revisions on purpose: REAPER's native RENDER_STATS program measure -- `analysis.meter`'s program loudness and every deliverable-spec check -- is BS.1770-5, and the in-box C++ gated engine that measures stems, objects, the isolated dialog bus and folds that exist only in memory is BS.1770-4, pinned to it by unit test (Table 1's RLB numerator and Tables 4/5's channel weights). The word "throughout" was the only false statement. No engine changed and no measurement moves.
`README.md` claimed CI builds the macOS / Windows / Linux matrix on every push. It does not: CI is Ubuntu-only on push, and the three-OS matrix runs on a version tag or a manual dispatch.
`docs/MANUAL.md` hedged on the published ReaPack index URL. It now states it, and states the macOS signing posture plainly: the binary is ad-hoc codesigned -- the signature Apple Silicon requires to load it at all -- and is not notarized.
Surface 190 tools / 4 resources / 5 prompts -- UNMOVED. ctest 28, unmoved.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
Hygiene release: a user-facing warning no longer cites an internal engineering document.
`analysis.meter`'s CROSS_NO_SIBLING warning -- the one that fires when a digital-silence render has no independent read path to check it against -- carried a parenthetical citation to an internal document. The sentence is unchanged in meaning; the citation is removed.
Surface 190 tools / 4 resources / 5 prompts -- UNMOVED. Unit suite 28, unmoved.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
Refusal release: `analysis.meter` will no longer REPORT a digital silence that two independent read paths disagree about over the same bounded window.
`analysis.meter` renders to measure. When that render comes back all-zero the tool used to report the silence as a measurement, and a dead render path is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from a genuinely silent one -- the same `-144.0` on every channel, the same `rawStats` carrying `LENGTH` alone, no `error` key, and elapsed times that do not discriminate either. The tool now cross-reads the same window through `analysis.accessor_meter`, which reads the track without rendering, and when the two paths disagree it refuses the CLAIM rather than the call: `render_silent_unconfirmed`. Pass `allowSilent` and it reports anyway, attaching BOTH readings and `windowMatched` so the disagreement is in the payload rather than in a footnote.
Two things it deliberately does NOT do. It does not refuse when the two reads covered DIFFERENT windows -- an unmatched window downgrades the refusal to a report and says so, because two readings over different windows are not a comparison. And it does not treat "the accessor sees content" as proof the render is dead: the accessor reads PRE track FX, volume and pan, so a MUTED track legitimately reads content and renders to silence.
The warning now names WHICH branch produced the cross-read, as `crossRead.pathKind`: `accessor_read`, `accessor_failed`, or `no_sibling_path`. It previously selected on a bare availability boolean, so a read whose accessor path EXISTED AND FAILED was reported as "no independent read path exists for this target" -- the right verdict attached to the wrong reason. A fail-closed fourth branch names an unaccounted state rather than borrowing the nearest plausible one.
*** Behaviour change: a call that previously returned a silent measurement can now refuse. *** Pass allowSilent:true for the previous behaviour, with both readings attached.
Surface 190 tools / 4 resources / 5 prompts -- UNMOVED. ctest 28, unmoved.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog:
Instrument release: Inseglet can now tell you whether a take's media is actually there.
reaper://track/{trackIndex}/item/{itemIndex}/take/{takeIndex}/source is a new resource -- the fourth -- carrying a per-source readout for one take: the ReaScript-API rows (file name, type, channel count, sample rate, length) alongside the SDK vtable rows, including PCM_source::IsAvailable(). IsAvailable is not in the ReaScript API at any version, so this is the only route to a take's source-validity state: online, offline, or missing. Read vtable.controlPassed before any vtable row -- when it is false, the SDK header and the running REAPER disagree about the vtable layout and no vtable figure is believable. The panel carries that control itself rather than letting the numbers quietly lie.
The three accessor tools - analysis.accessor_meter, analysis.accessor_levels and analysis.accessor_gaps - now report source validity instead of papering over it. Each read gains a sourceValidity block: how many sources it interrogated, how many reported unavailable, the RAW sample rate / channel count / length the source gave, and `defaulted`, which NAMES every field a fallback stood in for. On a read that did not interrogate exactly one source - every track read - those three are NULL rather than 0, because a zero there would be the very substitution this release removes. When a source is unavailable the block also carries the remedy.
*** This is ADDITIVE. No tool changes what it returns, refuses anything it used to accept, or reads different samples. ***
The fix behind it is ours. The accessor substituted a plausible sample rate for a source that reported zero, and a channel count of 2 for one that reported less than one - exactly the two fields REAPER zeroes when it cannot open a source. So the read looked identical whether the media was there or not. A defensive default is a detector-killer: code that swaps a plausible value in for a missing one destroys the evidence that it was missing.
The predicate now lives in its own REAPER-free header so its whole truth table is testable, and unit.source_probe carries two controls that must FIRE: the pre-fix defaults reproducing the identical-read null, and the predicate stripped of its quarter-note guard reporting an ordinary MIDI take as a broken source. The second is the expensive direction - a detector that fires on healthy content is a detector its users switch off.
Surface 190 tools / 4 resources / 5 prompts (was 190 / 3 / 5). ctest 27 -> 28.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: Guard release: the ADM, DAMF and Loom export tools can now FAIL TO MEASURE. All three used to author a complete deliverable from a render in which every sample of every channel was exactly zero, stamping loudness claims that were just the arithmetic image of "no samples" (-120 dB RMS, a -70 LUFS floor, 0.0 active fraction). The old render_empty guard only caught a render of zero LENGTH. *** BREAKING: authoring a deliberately silent master now needs allowSilent:true. *** Passing allowSilent reproduces the previous bytes EXACTLY - the escape hatch is the old behaviour, verified byte-identical on three fixtures. Surface is unchanged at 190 tools / 3 resources / 5 prompts, but THREE TOOLS GAIN ONE PARAMETER - a schema change the tool-count triple cannot see. The test is exact zero on every sample of every channel, never a threshold: a real 7.1.4 deliverable with one channel fed has ELEVEN of twelve channels on the same floor triple, so a per-channel rule would reject real work. One 1e-9 sample clears the guard. Whether a quiet master is too quiet is not this tool's judgement to make, and the -70 floor is correct and stays. It was never one site: export_damf authored its triad from the same unmeasured render, and export_loom_manifest emitted the same floor triple through intentFillLevels / intentBedLufs plus a whole-bed expectLufs of -70. Measured pre-fix on all three. docs/REFERENCE.md is regenerated: allowSilent had existed in three input schemas and in no user-facing document, because the surface gate counts tools, not parameters.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: Correctness release: our BS.1770-4 RLB filter was non-conformant, and every loudness figure Inseglet has ever reported read LOW by a constant. Surface UNCHANGED (190 tools / 3 resources / 5 prompts) - no new verbs, no new parameters. *** THIS BREAKS NUMERIC COMPARABILITY WITH v1.9.0 AND EARLIER for ABSOLUTE loudness. *** Figures reported by any prior release are low by 0.047099 / 0.043277 / 0.023566 / 0.021652 LU at 44.1 / 48 / 88.2 / 96 kHz. RELATIVE quantities - channel balances, deltas, ratios, LRA, activity fractions - are unaffected, because the correction is a pure gain at every frequency and the shift cancels. Add the constant for your sample rate to compare archived absolute figures against v1.10.0 output. The K-weighting stage-2 (RLB) highpass divided its numerator by a0, forcing the passband gain to exactly 1.000000000000. BS.1770-4 Table 1 keeps that numerator as exactly [1, -2, 1] - it is not normalised - and its gain is a0 = 1.004994898715 at 48 kHz. The -0.691 calibration term is defined against the TABULATED filter, so the normalised form read low by the constant above at every frequency. Moved by the fix: analysis.meter's channelsDetail[].kLevelLkfs, accessor_meter, object_loudness, stem_loudness, dialog_loudness, downmix_loudness, gatedLoudness() and the intent sidecar's expectLufs claims. The K-weighting shelf gain constant was also truncated to 12 significant digits where the reference carries 16, reaching b1 as a 1.044942e-12 error against Table 1. Worth about 3.3e-12 LU - below every measurement - but it was the whole of a discrepancy that had been attributed to the table's own precision rather than to us. Verified live against a running REAPER on 28 windows: the shift reproduced to 3.5e-12 LU and the cross-engine residual column came back invariant to 3.5e-12 LU. Cross-checked against a second independent BS.1770-4 implementation on 13 rows: the two now agree to 1.7799e-12 LU, where before the fix they differed by exactly the constant above - with Inseglet on the low side and the other implementation conformant. unit.meter now gates all five coefficients of BOTH filter stages against Table 1 at 1e-12, with a negative control that rejects the pre-fix numerator. The previous check gated the K-curve against flatness at 1 kHz to +/- 1.2 dB, which is 28x too loose to see a 0.043 dB error.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: Correctness release: 7.1.2 bed loudness, the identity-tone cache, and a routing detector that had been reporting false faults on 22.2. Surface UNCHANGED (190 tools / 3 resources / 5 prompts) - this release adds one parameter and no verbs. analysis.verify_routing gave FALSE VERDICTS on 22.2. 22.2 is the only bed layout declaring two LFE slots, and the plan put the one 40 Hz LFE tone on both, so the tone set was not unique. A PERFECTLY ROUTED 24-channel render came back ok=false, with channel 3 "bleed" at a margin of exactly 0.000000000 dB and channel 9 "duplicated", both at planCoverage 1.000000 - nothing in the numbers signalled it. Reaching it required doing exactly what the tool's own description instructs (passing back the echoed lfeChannels); with them omitted the same width read a clean 24/24, which is why it went unseen. The detector now REFUSES a degenerate plan outright and returns NO per-channel verdicts, rather than attaching a warning to a wrong answer. 7.1.2 beds received NO BS.1770-4 channel weights, reading 0.350 LU LOW. bedChannelLabels() enumerated cases 1/2/6/8/12/16 with no case 10, while the LFE predicate beside it generalised - so a layout the product accepts silently lost its weights while reporting "multichannel". 7.1.2 is the default bedLayout in three spatial tool schemas, and the bed.expectLufs claim consumed by iamf-sentinel-pro's intent-compare inherited the error. spatial.inject_identity_tones advertised "7.1.2" in its own schema enum and then refused it at runtime. Every bed-layout width now derives from ONE canonical table; five hand-rolled per-consumer width mappings are deleted. A registry-walking guard asserts that every layout any tool advertises is accepted at runtime, so a tool written later is covered by default. spatial.inject_identity_tones served STALE AUDIO after a parameter change. Files were named by slot index alone, so two calls with different parameters shared one path; REAPER installs a per-path PCM cache on the second access, and from then on a rewrite of that path is invisible - the tool reported the parameters it was asked for while REAPER played the earlier audio. Filenames now carry a hash of the WAV bytes, so identical parameters still give identical paths (determinism holds, and the cache hit is then correct) while different parameters can no longer collide at all. NEW: spatial.inject_identity_tones gains constantHz - one frequency on every slot, LFE included, so a multichannel fixture can hold a single frequency. The 313 + 139k plan cannot express that. A plan carrying it is a level instrument, not a routing one, and the routing detector refuses it by construction.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: IAMF ingest + in-DAW QC (190 tools / 3 resources / 5 prompts; was 187 / 3 / 4). spatial.export_adm now emits every audioObject before any audioChannelFormat, fixing a whole-file rejection by iamf-tools' ADM importer ("Failed to parse gain") — v1.7.0 exports were refused outright. No emitted byte changed, only the order the three groups are joined. New dolbyMetadataChunk:"placeholder" (default "none", and INDEPENDENT of profile) emits a placeholder `dbmd` chunk AND renames the bed to Dolby's RoomCentric* vocabulary — one switch, because a consumer only reads those names when a `dbmd` is present — so the importer keeps the objects instead of failing the encode with "No audioObject present". It fails closed, with the remedy named, on non-24-bit, a rate outside {48k, 96k}, or a bed outside 5.1 / 7.1 / 7.1.2, and a runtime advisory discloses the trade on four surfaces. New author_dolby_adm prompt (5th). spatial.inject_identity_tones + analysis.verify_routing: in-DAW channel-identity QC. A unique tone per bed channel or object track (313 + 139k Hz, LFE 40 Hz, -18 dBFS) read back from a rendered WAV or a render-free track accessor, reporting identity / swapped / duplicated / dropped / bleed / silent per channel with a measured margin — catches the routing fault class inside the session, before export, and independently verifies Inseglet's own send encodings. envelope.ensure_fx_envelope: ensures an FX-parameter envelope exists and returns the name envelope.add_point looks up (add_point could only write to an already-active envelope, and autoActivate reaches only REAPER's built-in track envelopes). Tiered parameter resolution that refuses an ambiguous request by naming its candidates instead of silently picking one.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: B1 intent sidecar (authoring side) + representation-aware positioning. No surface-count change (187 tools / 3 resources / 4 prompts). intentSidecar: true on spatial.export_adm and spatial.export_loom_manifest writes the session's own predictions beside the export (<base>.intent.json / manifest.intent.json, schema intent: 0): per-channel bed level claims (BS.1770-4-conformant whole-bed weights), object trajectories at block reach times, SN3D projection-decode dominance/coverage predictions, per-ACN scene RMS. Never a declared deliverable loudness — every level is an expect* claim for the open iamf-sentinel-pro consumer (sentinel intent-compare, S-340..S-346). Silent-channel claims floor at the BS.1770 silence convention (-70 LKFS), verified through a live REAPER -> export -> consumer gate. spatial.set_source_position now drives azimuth/elevation on angle-representation panners (IEM/SPARTA-style encoders) instead of bare-letter param matching, which could land on Quaternion X — or read "aZimuth" as z — and move params the ADM exporter never samples; ReaSurroundPan-style cartesian writes are unchanged, and auto-detect finds angle panners without an explicit fx index.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: IAMF delivery: the Loom bridge + cross-ecosystem docs (187 tools / 3 resources / 4 prompts; includes the 1.5.1 correctness patch). spatial.export_loom_manifest: one call renders the session's bed (stereo/5.1/7.1.4) and/or ambisonic scene (order 1-4, ACN/SN3D) plus per-language VO stems as 48 kHz integer-PCM WAVs in iamf-loom's channel order and emits the loom: 0 manifest (+ optional season.yaml); `loom compile` accepts the output as-is and every packaged deliverable is gated by the iamf-sentinel validator. Channel mapping is identity (spelling-only label deltas), verified with per-channel identity tones. Never writes a loudness value (Loom measures); objects fail closed to the ADM route (spatial.export_adm). New deliver_to_iamf expert prompt (4th) walks inventory -> per-mix channel-budget check (the M-416 class) -> dryRun preview -> export -> loom compile/run. New MANUAL section 9 "Delivering to IAMF" documents the pipeline end to end.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: Correctness-first patch release; no surface change (186 tools). BS.1770-4 bed channel weights now read Tables 4/5 exactly (boundary-inclusive: 1.41 only at ear level within |az| 60-120): rear surrounds Lsr/Rsr (M+/-135) 1.41 -> 1.00; wides Lw/Rw (M+/-060, 9.1.6) 1.00 -> 1.41. Every loudness tool inherits; 7.1-family readings move <= ~1.5 dB of affected-channel contribution; 5.1/stereo/22.2 unchanged. ADM hardening: writer azimuth wrap + elevation clamp + distance floor at spherical serialization; LFE <frequency> at its BS.2076 home (audioChannelFormat); real ds64.riffSize on BW64. adm_profile_check now classifies common-definitions ADM (previously invisible: HOA/binaural/multi-programme/oversize beds correctly non-conformant), gates bed layouts against the BS.2094 table, enforces single-programme + 24-bit, and verifies the interpolationLength ramp (new code: interpolation_ramp). adm_inspect gains a per-channel summary + packTypes census and a corrected version readout.

version.author: James Livingston
version.changelog: First public macOS release. In-process MCP server (Streamable HTTP + SSE, JSON-RPC 2.0, MCP 2025-06-18); loopback-only transport with a bearer token; every mutation single-undo. 186 tools / 3 resources / 3 prompts, with immersive/spatial audio as the differentiator: channel beds (5.1–22.2), ambisonic encode/decode + order/format conversion (ACN/SN3D), surround panners, binaural monitoring + live head-tracking; native ADM BWF and Dolby Atmos Master File (.atmos triad) authoring + inspection; bed/object send-layout orchestration for an external renderer; immersive metering (ITU-R BS.1770 loudness, DirAC/Gerzon spatial field, per-object loudness, decode-coverage + per-object decode-coverage timelines); deliverable-spec conformance; immersive style chains with a multichannel true-peak limiter; a composite macro DSL; and async MCP elicitation for destructive confirmation.

metadata.description: A native REAPER extension exposing a first-class Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface, with immersive / spatial audio as the primary differentiator. Loopback-only transport with a bearer token; every mutation is single-undo. macOS-first; Windows/Linux to follow once load-verified.
